raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
<!-- vLLM PR description format: Purpose / Test Plan / Test Result -->

## Purpose

Encoder CUDA graphs are captured once per token budget, and every captured graph allocates its own full set of I/O buffers sized by that budget. That per-budget O(budget) memory cost is the only reason the default budget table is a coarse power-of-2 ladder — which forces ~33% average padding waste (round-up to the next power of two).

This PR removes the memory cost **generically, with zero model changes**, following the decoder's `input_ids[:num_tokens]` pattern:

1. **Universal shared capture buffers.** At capture time the manager keeps the first (largest) budget's buffers per (path, axis) as the shared allocation; for every later budget it probes shapes via the model's unmodified `prepare_encoder_cudagraph_capture_inputs()` and, per buffer key, checks prefix compatibility (same ndim/trailing dims/dtype, rows fit). Compatible keys capture into a prefix view of the shared buffer (probe content is copied in so the capture-time forward sees correct metadata); incompatible keys silently keep their per-budget allocation. Scalars are shared by identity. This works because all encoder buffers are packed-contiguous row buffers and replay only ever writes `buf[:real_rows]`. Output buffers are shared the same way. No protocol changes, no model changes, no config knobs.

2. **Subdivided default budget table.** With extra graphs costing ~zero buffer memory, the auto-inferred default becomes a subdivided table (4 steps per octave up to 1024, 2 above; 64→16384 = 25 tiers, expected padding waste ~10% vs ~33% for power-of-2). Explicit `encoder_cudagraph_token_budgets` still overrides. Capture-time cost is one extra forward per extra tier; the existing 64-graph warning covers capture-axes blowups.

Duplicate-work check: no open PR covers encoder-graph buffer sharing; complements #41714 (pool memory in profiling) and follows the padding-semantics precedent of #42796.

## Test Plan

```bash
# Unit + capture/replay (GPU)
pytest tests/v1/cudagraph/test_encoder_cudagraph.py -q
# E2E incl. real-weights Qwen2.5-VL (image+video) and DSV4.1 dummy
pytest tests/models/multimodal/generation/test_vit_cudagraph.py -k "deepseek_v41 or qwen2_5_vl" -x -q
pre-commit run --files <changed files>
```

New coverage: `TestDefaultBudgetTable` (subdivided default, user override, `max_vision_items` path), `TestSharedCaptureBuffers` (one storage across budgets with a **completely unmodified** mock model, prefix views, shared output slicing, large→small→large replay equivalence vs eager, `clear()` releases), `TestSharedBufferFallback` (an incompatible-shaped buffer falls back to its own allocation while other keys still share; scalars shared by identity).

Performance measured on one idle 4×GB200 (SM100) Slurm node, TP=4, `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash` (dummy weights; timing is shape-exact), baseline/patched interleaved on the same node.

## Test Result

- `tests/v1/cudagraph/test_encoder_cudagraph.py`: **80 passed** (GPU).
- e2e: **3 passed, 1 skipped** (DSV4.1 video skip is pre-existing upstream).

### Capture cost (DSV4.1, TP=4, per-rank)

| Run | Budget table | Encoder graphs | Capture memory | Capture time |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Upstream default | pow2, 9 tiers | 9 | 4.19 GiB | 14 s |
| **This PR (default)** | **25 tiers, subdivided** | **25** | **3.80 GiB** | 21 s |

The dense table's 16 extra graphs cost zero buffer memory, and total capture memory ends up *below* the upstream default (Σbudgets ≈ 2×max → 1×max for encoder buffers) at a one-time +7 s capture cost.

### Request latency (concurrency-1 probes, medians of interleaved rounds)

| Probe | pow2 | this PR | Change |
|---|---|---|---|
| pad2_heavy: 5×1344² imgs, 5120 tok (8192 → 6144 tier) | 577.9 / 570.2 ms | 569.0 / 553.0 ms | ~-2-3% |
| mid_pad: 1×714² img (512 → 320 tier) | 134.6 / 136.6 ms | 138.7 / 135.9 ms | neutral |
| no_pad control (994 tok → 1024 both) | 211.4 / 214.8 ms | 223.0 / 215.7 ms | neutral |
| cliff_900 (508 tok → 512 tier both) | 159.6 / 157.3 ms | 162.0 / 156.5 ms | neutral |

VisionArena-Chat TTFT at concurrency 1: medians identical (~127-129 ms); means are dominated by warmup-order noise (an established property of this benchmark on this cluster).

### Notes / caveats

- The latency win scales with per-batch padding; high-padding workloads (multi-image requests landing just above a power of two) gain a few percent, everything else is neutral. The structural point of this PR is making fine-grained budgets free (memory), not the probe numbers.
- Prefix-incompatible buffers (hypothetical; none among the 21 current encoder-CG models) degrade gracefully to per-budget allocation.
- `docs/design/cuda_graphs_multimodal.md` is updated accordingly.

---

AI assistance disclosure: this change was developed with AI assistance (Kimi Code). The human submitter reviewed every changed line; tests and benchmarks were run as listed above.


---

<summary> Pull Request Checklist </summary>

- [ ] I used vLLM's `/pr-checklist` skill. (Mandatory for agents, optional for humans).
- [ ] AI assistance was used during the creation of this PR.

- [ ] **Design Fit:** Minimizes impact on core components, reuses existing functionality, and justifies added complexity.
- [ ] **Testing and Validation:** Validates the change and ensures any added tests are meaningful and reliable, with CI coverage or documented CI resource constraints and validation performed outside CI.
- [ ] **Code Quality and Style:** Keeps code and comments clear and concise, and updates relevant documentation and examples.
- [ ] **Pull Request Contents:** Includes a brief summary and relevant links, supports claims with evidence, explains root causes and implementation trade-offs, and follows the contributing guide.
</details>

End-to-end serving numbers for this PR on MiniMax-M3 (MI355X, TP2, `--mm-encoder-tp-mode data`), in case they are useful.

**Summary.** With the default budgets, this PR's head (`d9d886a5d`) serves MiniMax-M3 about as fast as main's defaults:
- **Throughput:** +0.7% over 8 image rows, inside the run-to-run noise of 1.2%.
- **2048x1600 images:** −0.8%. The 4163-token image is now padded to 6144 instead of 8192.
- **Encoder-graph memory:** 16.85 vs 16.86 GiB per rank, so 27 budgets with shared buffers cost the same as main's 10.
- **Accuracy:** MMMU 0.6489.

Compared with our hand-tuned budget list, it is −0.8% overall and −6.1% on 2048x1600, with 7% fewer KV-cache tokens. With #65227 on top, the defaults beat our hand-tuned list. Numbers are posted on #65227.

| arm (2 passes each) | throughput, 8 rows vs main default | 2048x1600 throughput vs main default | encoder budgets | graph memory per rank (TP0/TP1) | KV-cache tokens | MMMU val |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| main default budgets | — | — | 10, 64..32768 | 16.86 / 17.55 GiB | 3,850,240 | — |
| **this PR, default budgets** | **+0.7%** | **−0.8%** | 27, 64..32768 | 16.85 / 17.54 GiB | 3,854,336 | 0.6489 |
| this PR + #65227, default budgets | +2.9% | +6.5% | 17 kept by the startup probe | 5.74 / 6.43 GiB | 4,165,632 | 0.6500 |
| main, hand-tuned budgets (64..3072, 14 graphs) | +1.6% | +5.7% | 14 | 6.46 / 7.15 GiB | 4,145,152 | 0.6444 |

Run-to-run noise (8-row throughput between an arm's two passes): 0.1–1.2%. Median TTFT/TPOT on these closed-loop rows varies a lot from pass to pass, so I left it out; the full table is in the details. Every arm also carries two of my own open changes, which are the same in all arms: #64928 (FP8 ViT attention on ROCm) and #65352 (the DP-ViT empty-rank fix).

Happy to rerun on a newer head after your rebase.

<details>
<summary>Setup, workload and full results</summary>

**Hardware and software.** One node with 8x AMD Instinct MI355X (gfx950); each server TP2 on one GPU pair, with servers
of different arms running at the same time on the node's four pairs. ROCm 7.15 (HIP runtime 7.16.26361), PyTorch 2.13.0.
vLLM: ROCm nightly image 0.33.0rc1.dev573+g40941f2c4 with a Python-only overlay ("base"): the `vllm/` files changed by
the 12 main commits up to `67791dd94` (these include #65226), #64928 commits 1-3 (FP8 ViT attention on ROCm, head_dim 80
padded to 128 with `VLLM_ROCM_VIT_FP8_PAD_HEAD_DIM=128`) and #65352 (DP-ViT empty-rank fix). Each arm adds only the listed
PRs' `vllm/` Python files (no docs or tests).

**Server** (identical in every arm except the image and `encoder_cudagraph_token_budgets`): `amd/MiniMax-M3-MXFP4-AttnFP8`,
`--tensor-parallel-size 2 --mm-encoder-tp-mode data --mm-encoder-attn-dtype fp8` (static FP8 scales),
`--kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3 --block-size 128 --max-num-seqs 128 --max-model-len 133120 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.95
--no-enable-prefix-caching --async-scheduling --attention-backend ROCM_AITER_UNIFIED_ATTN --moe-backend aiter`,
`-cc '{"mode": 3, "cudagraph_mode": "FULL_AND_PIECEWISE", "custom_ops": ["+rms_norm", "+quant_fp8"],
"cudagraph_mm_encoder": true}'` plus the budgets below, `--limit-mm-per-prompt '{"image": 1}'`,
`--mm-processor-kwargs '{"min_pixels": 65536, "max_pixels": 16777216}'`.

| arm | code | `encoder_cudagraph_token_budgets` |
|---|---|---|
| M | base | `[64, 128, 256, 384, 512, 640, 768, 1024, 1280, 1536, 1792, 2048, 2560, 3072]` |
| A0 | base | not set (default) |
| A1 | base + #65226 (already contained in base: A/A control of A0) | not set (default) |
| A2 | base + #65084 (`d9d886a5d`, `vllm/` files) | not set (default) |
| A3 | base + #65084 + #65227 (`76f9a2057`, `vllm/` files) | not set (default) |

**Workload.** SGLang `bench_serving` 0.5.18 (`--backend sglang-oai-chat --dataset-name image --image-count 1`, random

(2048x1600). Two passes per arm; each value is the geomean of the two passes. Output throughput: X/ref - 1; median TTFT

| arm | output throughput, 8-row geomean: vs M / vs A0 | median TTFT, 8 rows: vs M / vs A0 | median TPOT, 8 rows: vs M / vs A0 | row 15 (2048x1600) throughput: vs M / vs A0 | row 15 median TTFT: vs M / vs A0 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| M | - / +1.6% | - / +3.5% | - / -3.3% | - / +5.7% | - / +20.5% |
| A0 | -1.6% / - | -3.4% / - | +3.4% / - | -5.4% / - | -17.0% / - |
| A1 | -2.0% / -0.4% | +2.2% / +5.8% | +1.9% / -1.5% | -5.5% / -0.2% | -14.1% / +3.5% |
| A2 | -0.8% / +0.7% | +0.6% / +4.2% | -3.3% / -6.4% | -6.1% / -0.8% | -5.9% / +13.4% |

Run-to-run noise: spread of the 8-row throughput geomean between an arm's two passes: M 0.6%, A0 0.1%, A1 0.9%, A2 1.2%, A3 0.6%. A1 vs A0 (same code, A/A, 8-row geomeans): -0.4% throughput, +5.8% median TTFT, -1.5% median TPOT.

| arm | encoder graph budgets | encoder graphs captured per rank (TP0/TP1) | graph memory per rank, GiB (encoder + decoder graphs, TP0/TP1) | KV cache tokens | MMMU val (900 questions) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| M | `[64, 128, 256, 384, 512, 640, 768, 1024, 1280, 1536, 1792, 2048, 2560, 3072]` | 14/14 | 6.46/7.15; 6.47/7.15 | 4,145,152 | 0.6444 (stderr 0.0149) |
| A0 | default: 10 budgets, 64..32768 | 10/10 | 16.86/17.55 | 3,850,240 | not run |
| A1 | default: 10 budgets, 64..32768 | 10/10 | 16.86/17.55 | 3,850,240 | not run |
| A2 | default: 27 budgets, 64..32768 | 27/27 | 16.85/17.54 | 3,854,336 | 0.6489 (stderr 0.0148) |
| A3 | default: 27 budgets at init, startup probe kept (p1: TP0 64..1024, TP1 64..1024; p2: TP0 64..1024, TP1 64..1536) | 17/17; 17/18 | 5.74/6.43; 5.74/6.66 | 4,165,632; 4,161,536 | 0.6500 (stderr 0.0146) |

Notes:
- vLLM logs encoder and decoder CUDA graph memory together ("Graph capturing finished ... took X GiB"); the decoder graphs are the same in every arm, so the differences between arms are encoder-graph memory. The KV cache is sized after graph capture, so graph memory comes out of the KV cache. No row comes near the KV capacity (row 21: ~0.54M tokens in flight).
- M runs 2048x1600 (4163 tokens) eagerly (above its largest budget 3072); A0 and A1 pad it to 8192, A2 to 6144; A3's startup probe runs it eagerly. The probe is timed at startup and is per rank (with `--mm-encoder-tp-mode data` each rank encodes its own images); its cut point differed between A3's passes and between the ranks of pass 2.
- MMMU val via lm_eval 0.4.13 through the server's chat API; M's value is from a run of the same M configuration on 2026-11-03.
</details>

+    def _generate_budgets(
+        min_budget: int,
+        max_budget: int,
+    ) -> list[int]:
+        """Generate token budgets from min_budget to max_budget.
+
+        Subdivided grid: quarter-octave steps up to 1024, half-octave steps
+        above. Capture buffers are shared across budgets (see
+        ``_capture_budget_graph``), so extra graphs cost no buffer memory
+        and the finer table only cuts padding waste.
+        """
+        points = {min_budget, max_budget}
+        base = 1
+        while base < max_budget:
+            # Quarter-octave grid below 1024, half-octave above.
+            steps = 4 if base < 1024 else 2
+            step = base // steps
+            for k in range(steps):
+                point = base + k * step
+                if min_budget <= point <= max_budget:
+                    points.add(point)
+            base *= 2
+        return sorted(points)

This pull request has merge conflicts that must be resolved before it can be
merged. Please rebase the PR, @Isotr0py.

https://docs.github.com/en/pull-requests/collaborating-with-pull-requests/working-with-forks/syncing-a-fork

End-to-end serving numbers for this PR on MiniMax-M3 (MI355X, TP2, `--mm-encoder-tp-mode data`), in case they are useful.

**Summary.** With the default budgets, this PR's head (`d9d886a5d`) serves MiniMax-M3 about as fast as main's defaults:
- **Throughput:** +0.7% over 8 image rows, inside the run-to-run noise of 1.2%.
- **2048x1600 images:** −0.8%. The 4163-token image is now padded to 6144 instead of 8192.
- **Encoder-graph memory:** 16.85 vs 16.86 GiB per rank, so 27 budgets with shared buffers cost the same as main's 10.
- **Accuracy:** MMMU 0.6489.

Compared with our hand-tuned budget list, it is −0.8% overall and −6.1% on 2048x1600, with 7% fewer KV-cache tokens. With #65227 on top, the defaults beat our hand-tuned list. Numbers are posted on #65227.

| arm (2 passes each) | throughput, 8 rows vs main default | 2048x1600 throughput vs main default | encoder budgets | graph memory per rank (TP0/TP1) | KV-cache tokens | MMMU val |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| main default budgets | — | — | 10, 64..32768 | 16.86 / 17.55 GiB | 3,850,240 | — |

| main, hand-tuned budgets (64..3072, 14 graphs) | +1.6% | +5.7% | 14 | 6.46 / 7.15 GiB | 4,145,152 | 0.6444 |

Run-to-run noise (8-row throughput between an arm's two passes): 0.1–1.2%. Median TTFT/TPOT on these closed-loop rows varies a lot from pass to pass, so I left it out; the full table is in the details. Every arm also carries two of my own open changes, which are the same in all arms: #64928 (FP8 ViT attention on ROCm) and #65352 (the DP-ViT empty-rank fix).

Happy to rerun on a newer head after your rebase.

Run-to-run noise: spread of the 8-row throughput geomean between an arm's two passes: M 0.6%, A0 0.1%, A1 0.9%, A2 1.2%, A3 0.6%. A1 vs A0 (same code, A/A, 8-row geomeans): -0.4% throughput, +5.8% median TTFT, -1.5% median TPOT.

| A0 | default: 10 budgets, 64..32768 | 10/10 | 16.86/17.55 | 3,850,240 | not run |
| A1 | default: 10 budgets, 64..32768 | 10/10 | 16.86/17.55 | 3,850,240 | not run |

Notes:
- vLLM logs encoder and decoder CUDA graph memory together ("Graph capturing finished ... took X GiB"); the decoder graphs are the same in every arm, so the differences between arms are encoder-graph memory. The KV cache is sized after graph capture, so graph memory comes out of the KV cache. No row comes near the KV capacity (row 21: ~0.54M tokens in flight).
- M runs 2048x1600 (4163 tokens) eagerly (above its largest budget 3072); A0 and A1 pad it to 8192, A2 to 6144; A3's startup probe runs it eagerly. The probe is timed at startup and is per rank (with `--mm-encoder-tp-mode data` each rank encodes its own images); its cut point differed between A3's passes and between the ranks of pass 2.
- MMMU val via lm_eval 0.4.13 through the server's chat API; M's value is from a run of the same M configuration on 2026-11-03.
